structure.overview: The case concerns a Colombian appellant seeking refugee protection in Canada due to threats from the ELN, with the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejecting her claim based on a safe internal flight alternative (IFA) in Barranquilla. The appellant appealed the RPD's decision, submitting new evidence and challenging the findings on ELN's motivation and presence. The tribunal dismissed the appeal, agreeing with the RPD that the appellant has a viable IFA and is not at serious risk of persecution, and rejected the new evidence as inadmissible.

party_points.text: Fears ELN extortion threats and seeks protection
Post-RPD report on IFA viability as new evidence
ELN's presence in Atlántico and major cities means potential targeting
ELN's lack of pursuit in 2016 doesn't prove lack of motivation; criticizes assumptions about family targeting

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Appellant, a Colombian citizen, fears returning due to ELN extortion threats and fled to Canada seeking protection.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The RPD rejected the Appellant's claim due to a safe internal flight alternative (IFA) in Barranquilla; the Appellant appeals this finding.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal finds the key issue is IFA and agrees the RPD correctly found a viable IFA in Barranquilla.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The appeal is dismissed; the RPD was correct that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Under IRPA s.110(4) and jurisprudence, new evidence must be post-RPD, unavailable before, and credible, relevant, and new to be accepted.

citations.cite: subsection 110(4) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA)
citations.why: Sets criteria for accepting new evidence on appeal

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Appellant submits a post-RPD report on IFA viability, arguing it responds to RPD's incorrect findings and was not reasonably available earlier.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal rejects the Appellant's argument, finding the report is inadmissible as it relies on pre-RPD events and was reasonably available before.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Appellant's unawareness of the report's availability is insufficient; she had notice and opportunity to present IFA evidence before the RPD.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Jurisprudence states new evidence is not to supplement deficient RPD records; claimants must present all available evidence initially.

citations.why: Federal Court on purpose of new evidence at RAD

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The report is inadmissible under s.110(4) and rejected; no oral hearing will be held.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: No new evidence accepted; thus, no oral hearing will be held under IRPA s.110(6).

citations.why: Conditions for oral hearing at RAD

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal's role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD's decision was correct.

citations.why: Role of RAD in reviewing RPD decisions

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RPD found the key issue was IFA viability; it concluded the Appellant would not face serious persecution in Barranquilla and relocation is reasonable.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Federal Court's two-pronged test for IFA viability requires no serious persecution risk and that relocation is not unreasonable.

citations.why: Federal Court's test for IFA viability

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Once an IFA is proposed, the claimant must prove it fails one or both prongs of the IFA test.

citations.why: Onus on claimant to disprove IFA viability

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: After review, the tribunal agrees with the RPD that the Appellant has a safe and viable IFA in Barranquilla.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RPD found ELN may not have strong presence or motivation to target the Appellant in Atlántico, where Barranquilla is located.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RPD found ELN did not pursue the Appellant in Popayan in 2016, indicating lack of motivation to target her.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RPD noted Appellant's family in Popayan were not pursued by ELN and found insufficient evidence linking brother's death to ELN.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RPD found ELN's extortion motive ceased as the Appellant's business is no longer operating.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RPD concluded insufficient evidence exists that ELN has means and motivation to seek the Appellant in Barranquilla.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Appellant argues ELN's presence in Atlántico and major cities means they could target her, challenging RPD's plausibility finding.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Appellant contends ELN's lack of pursuit in 2016 doesn't prove lack of motivation and criticizes assumptions about targeting family members as speculative.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal finds the RPD correctly concluded insufficient evidence shows ELN's motivation to pursue the Appellant in Barranquilla.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal rejects the Appellant's claim that RPD made plausibility findings, explaining plausibility relates to credibility of past facts.

citations.why: Definition and limits of plausibility findings

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The RPD assessed future risk evidence, not plausibility of past events, focusing on serious possibility of persecution in the IFA.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal agrees with the RPD that the evidence does not establish a serious possibility of persecution risk for the Appellant in Barranquilla.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Even if ELN is present and the Appellant a potential target, the agents' behavior shows no motivation to pursue her in Barranquilla.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The ELN's failure to pursue the Appellant's family, despite threats, indicates lack of ongoing motivation to target her.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal agrees with the RPD that there is insufficient evidence linking the brother's death to the ELN or the Appellant's case.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal agrees with the RPD that the ELN's lost motivation for extortion is relevant since the Appellant no longer operates her business.

citations.cite: Exhibit RPD-1, RPD Record, Exhibit 4, p. 38, para. 2; Transcript of September 23, 2021, RPD Hearing, pp. 8, 11
citations.why: Evidence of ELN's extortion demand and Appellant's testimony

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal finds insufficient evidence of serious persecution risk from the ELN given the Appellant's circumstances and that the proposed IFA is reasonable.

citations.cite: Ibid., Exhibit 3, National Documentation Package (NDP) for Colombia, (31 August 2021), item 7.37, pages 3-11
citations.why: Objective evidence about ELN and risk factors

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal moves from assessing the first prong of the IFA test to considering the second prong of reasonableness.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The RPD considered the Appellant's circumstances on the second prong despite no objections and found relocation hardships not unreasonable.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal agrees with the RPD that the evidence does not show it would be objectively unreasonable for the Appellant to relocate to Barranquilla.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The RPD correctly found the Appellant has a viable IFA in Barranquilla.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The tribunal dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD's decision that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.

citations.cite: M.C.I. v. Singh, Parminder (F.C.A., no. A-512-14), Nadon, Gauthier, de Montigny, March 29, 2016, 2016 FCA 96
Raza, Syed Masood v. M.C.I. (F.C.A., no. A-11-07), Linden, Sharlow, Ryer, December 6, 2007, 2007 FCA 385
